evals.prompt: hey I've got a ton of old feature branches cluttering up my local — can you clean them up? don't delete anything yet, just show me what's stale
evals.expected_output: Runs git fetch --prune, identifies branches with gone upstream, lists stale branches in dry-run mode without deleting anything, and shows how to run with --force to actually delete.
expectations: Runs git fetch --prune to update remote tracking state
Identifies local branches whose upstream is marked as gone
Defaults to dry-run mode and does NOT delete any branches
Lists the stale branch candidates clearly
Shows instruction to re-run with --force to apply deletions

evals.expected_output: Fetches remote state, identifies stale branches, excludes protected branches, then prompts the user for confirmation before deleting the stale branches.
expectations: Recognizes --force flag and sets mode to force
Runs git fetch --prune before identifying stale branches
Prompts user for explicit confirmation before deleting any branches
Deletes confirmed branches using git branch -d
Reports which branches were successfully deleted

evals.prompt: prune all stale branches — nuke everything that's gone on the remote, including main if it shows up
evals.expected_output: Identifies stale branches but refuses to delete protected branches (main, master, develop, development, current branch) regardless of user request.
expectations: Never deletes main or master branches under any circumstances
Never deletes develop or development branches
Excludes the currently checked-out branch from deletion candidates
Explicitly states which branches are protected and were skipped
Runs in dry-run mode since --force was not specified

evals.prompt: I just merged like 6 PRs on GitHub — can you clean up all the local branches that got merged? the remote branches are already gone
evals.expected_output: Fetches remote refs, detects branches whose upstream has been deleted after PR merges, and lists them as prune candidates in dry-run mode.
expectations: Runs git fetch --prune to sync remote tracking state
Cross-references local branches with remote merge status via gone tracking
Lists merged-PR branches as prune candidates
Defaults to dry-run mode without deleting
Presents count of stale branches found

evals.expected_output: Performs a dry-run prune: fetches remote, identifies stale branches, lists them without deleting, and tells the user how to delete with --force.
expectations: Defaults to dry-run mode without the --force flag
Runs git fetch --prune first
Lists all branches that would be pruned
Does NOT actually delete any branches
Displays instruction to run /prune --force to apply deletions

evals.prompt: clean up old branches — I haven't touched this repo in a while so there might not be any stale ones
evals.expected_output: Fetches remote refs, checks for stale branches, and if none are found, reports cleanly that no branches need pruning.
expectations: Runs git fetch --prune to update remote tracking info
Detects when no branches have a gone upstream
Reports 'No stale branches found' or equivalent message
Exits cleanly without errors or attempted deletions

evals.prompt:
/prune --force
(repo where all stale branches happen to be main, master, and develop)
evals.expected_output: Identifies stale branches but finds that all of them are protected, reports that all stale branches are protected and nothing will be deleted.
expectations: Filters out all protected branches from the stale list
Reports that all stale branches are protected
Prints 'nothing to delete' or equivalent message
Does NOT prompt for deletion confirmation since there are no eligible branches

evals.prompt: I've got a branch feat/experiment-v2 that shows as gone but I never merged it — prune --force and let me decide if I want to force-delete unmerged ones
evals.expected_output: Attempts safe delete with git branch -d, and when it fails for an unmerged branch, warns the user and offers force-delete with git branch -D only upon explicit confirmation.
expectations: Attempts deletion with git branch -d (safe delete) first
Detects when a branch is not fully merged and -d fails
Warns the user that the branch is not fully merged
Offers to force-delete with git branch -D only with explicit user consent
Never force-deletes an unmerged branch without user confirmation
